text: Imagine warming up a leftover hard boiled egg in the microwave.
It comes out looking totally normal.
But the second your fork touches it the egg blows apart with a bang.
One man bit into a microwaved egg at a restaurant and it burst in his mouth.
So two sound engineers heated almost a hundred eggs to see how loud they get.
They set each one on the floor by a microphone and stabbed it with a meat thermometer.
The loudest one was as loud as a jet plane a hundred feet away.
The engineers think the trick is hiding inside the yolk.
Tiny drops of water get trapped in the cooked yolk and heat up past boiling without turning to steam.
When you poke it one drop flashes to steam and sets off all the others at once.
So the egg doesn't crack. It boils apart from the inside.
Only about one in three eggs blew up so you never know which one will.
One of the engineers called it egg roulette.
Share this with someone who microwaves their eggs and subscribe for more.
